themes_detail.label: Park Noise Explosion
themes_detail.summary: Noise complaints from parks in CD 302 spiked to 4 complaints THIS WEEK compared to a baseline of 0.1 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3100% increase (z-score: 11.72)—suggesting a sudden, acute disruption at a specific park location that warrants immediate investigation.
evidence: 4 park noise complaints this week vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 11.72 indicates extreme statistical deviation
Signal emerged within last 7 days, indicating newly emerging problem
reporting_angles: Which park is generating complaints and what is the source of noise (events, construction, concerts)?
Interview affected residents about timing and duration of disturbances
Check Parks Department calendar for permitted events or construction activity

themes_detail.label: Construction Lead Dust Spike
themes_detail.summary: Construction lead dust complaints jumped to 4 THIS WEEK versus a baseline of 0.5 per week—an 700% increase (z-score: 4.95)—coinciding with 1234 active DOB building permits (881 alterations), suggesting active construction is exposing residents to lead hazards.
evidence: 4 lead dust complaints this week vs. 0.5 weekly average
1234 active DOB permits, including 881 alterations, indicating widespread construction
Z-score of 4.95 and timing suggests correlation with permit surge
reporting_angles: Cross-reference the 4 lead dust complaints with specific addresses and DOB permit data to identify problem construction sites
Interview residents in affected buildings about respiratory impacts and EPA notification requirements
Investigate DOB inspection protocols for lead abatement during renovation work

themes_detail.label: Outdoor Dining Complaints Surge
themes_detail.summary: Outdoor dining complaints increased to 3 THIS WEEK from a baseline of 0.4 per week—a 700% spike (z-score: 3.77)—suggesting emerging conflict over sidewalk space, noise, or operations of expanded dining areas, potentially linked to ongoing ULURP development activity.
evidence: 3 outdoor dining complaints this week vs. 0.4 weekly average over prior 8 weeks
Z-score of 3.77 indicates statistically significant deviation
Timing coincides with active ULURP applications (395 Flatbush, Columbia Heights rezoning) that may increase commercial density
reporting_angles: Identify which restaurants/locations are triggering complaints (sidewalk obstruction, noise, overflow crowds)
Interview community board and residents about tension between outdoor dining expansion and pedestrian access
Cross-check with 700% spike in Noise - Residential complaints (1732 total) to see if outdoor dining is a contributing factor

themes_detail.label: Electrical System Failures
themes_detail.summary: Electrical complaints spiked to 6 TWO WEEKS AGO versus a baseline of 1.0 per week—a 500% increase (z-score: 5.0)—indicating possible widespread electrical infrastructure stress or power delivery issues affecting multiple buildings.
evidence: 6 electrical complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 1.0 weekly baseline
Z-score of 5.0 indicates strong statistical significance
May correlate with 881 active building alterations that could stress grid
reporting_angles: Contact Con Edison about any reported outages, brownouts, or infrastructure work in CD 302 during the spike period
Interview residents about power outages or electrical failures and duration
Investigate whether old building stock in Brooklyn Heights or Fort Greene is experiencing aging infrastructure failures

themes_detail.label: Dead/Dying Trees Emerge
themes_detail.summary: Dead or dying tree complaints increased to 7 LAST WEEK versus a baseline of 1.2 per week—a 460% spike (z-score: 5.28)—suggesting possible disease, recent storm damage, or deferred maintenance at a specific location or across multiple sites.
evidence: 7 dead/dying tree complaints last week vs. 1.2 weekly average
Recurring budget request for Parks Department maintenance equipment suggests chronic underfunding of tree care
reporting_angles: Map the 7 complaints to identify if they cluster in one neighborhood (e.g., Fort Greene Park area) or are dispersed
Interview Parks Department about tree health monitoring and disease outbreak investigation
Check community board budget requests: repeated calls for Parks equipment maintenance suggest systemic resource shortage
